title: 09. Storage, CDN & Data Engineering: Data Pipelines, ETL/ELT & Stream Processing
summary: A data pipeline is an automated process that moves and transforms data from sources to destinations. Pipelines are the backbone of data engineering — they power analytics, ML models, dashboards, and data warehouses.

sections.title: Detailed Explanation
sections.body:
### What are Data Pipelines?

A **data pipeline** is an automated process that moves and transforms data from sources to destinations. Pipelines are the backbone of data engineering — they power analytics, ML models, dashboards, and data warehouses.

### ETL vs ELT

| Aspect             | ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) | ELT (Extract-Load-Transform) |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Transform location | Middle layer (Spark/Python)  | Inside data warehouse        |
| Best for           | Complex transformations      | SQL-based transformations    |
| Storage            | Only transformed data stored | Raw + transformed data       |
| Flexibility        | High (any language)          | Depends on warehouse SQL     |
| Examples           | Apache Spark, Airflow        | dbt + Snowflake/BigQuery     |

### Batch vs Stream Processing

| Feature    | Batch Processing     | Stream Processing                     |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Latency    | Minutes to hours     | Milliseconds to seconds               |
| Data       | Complete/bounded     | Continuous/unbounded                  |
| Processing | Process all at once  | Process as it arrives                 |
| Tools      | Spark, Hadoop, dbt   | Kafka Streams, Flink, Spark Streaming |
| Use case   | Reports, ML training | Real-time dashboards, fraud detection |

diagrams.title: Batch and streaming paths in a data platform
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  src["Apps, DB change logs (CDC), clickstream"] --> k[["Kafka"]]
  k --> stream["Stream processing: Flink / Spark Streaming"]
  stream --> rt[("Real-time store: dashboards, alerts")]
  k --> lake[("Data lake: raw files on S3")]
  lake --> batch["Batch ETL / ELT: Spark, dbt"]
  batch --> wh[("Warehouse: Snowflake, BigQuery")]
  wh --> bi["BI, reports, ML features"]
diagrams.explain: Events flow into Kafka once and feed two paths. The **streaming** path computes results within seconds for dashboards and alerts. The **batch** path lands raw data in a cheap lake and transforms it on a schedule into clean warehouse tables for reporting and ML. ELT — load first, transform inside the warehouse — is now the common default.

### ETL Pipeline Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          ETL PIPELINE                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  EXTRACT                    TRANSFORM                    LOAD
  ───────                    ─────────                    ────

  ┌──────────┐              ┌───────────────────┐        ┌────────────────┐
  │PostgreSQL│──┐           │                   │        │ Data Warehouse │
  └──────────┘  │           │  Clean            │        │ (Snowflake/    │
  ┌──────────┐  │  Raw      │  Validate         │  Clean │  BigQuery/     │
  │ MongoDB  │──┼─ Data ──▶│  Deduplicate      │─ Data ▶│  Redshift)     │
  └──────────┘  │           │  Aggregate        │        │                │
  ┌──────────┐  │           │  Join/Enrich      │        └────────────────┘
  │   APIs   │──┘           │  Format           │              │
  └──────────┘              └───────────────────┘        ┌─────┴──────────┐
  ┌──────────┐                    ▲                      │  Dashboards    │
  │  S3/GCS  │────────────────────┘                      │  ML Models     │
  └──────────┘                                           │  Reports       │
                                                         └────────────────┘
```

### Lambda Architecture (Batch + Real-time)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LAMBDA ARCHITECTURE                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                    ┌─────────────────────── BATCH LAYER ──────────────────┐
                    │                                                       │
  Data Sources ─────┤  Raw Data → Spark Batch → Data Warehouse             │
  (Kafka/Files)     │  (S3/HDFS)   (hourly)    (complete, accurate)        │
                    │                                                       │
                    ├───────────────── SPEED LAYER ────────────────────────┤
                    │                                                       │
                    │  Kafka → Flink/Spark Streaming → Real-time Store     │
                    │          (seconds)                 (Redis/Cassandra)  │
                    │          (approximate, fast)                          │
                    └───────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                                        ▼
                              ┌──────────────────┐
                              │   SERVING LAYER  │
                              │                  │
                              │  Query = Batch   │
                              │  results MERGED  │
                              │  with real-time  │
                              │  results         │
                              └──────────────────┘
```

### PySpark Pipeline Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      PYSPARK DATA PIPELINE                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Source                   Transformations                    Sink
  ──────                   ───────────────                    ────

  spark.read               df.filter()                      df.write
    .format("csv")           .select()                        .format("parquet")
    .load("s3://...")         .groupBy().agg()                 .mode("overwrite")
       │                      .join()                          .save("s3://...")
       ▼                      .withColumn()                         │
  ┌──────────┐                .dropDuplicates()              ┌──────┴─────┐
  │DataFrame │ ──▶ Lazy ──▶ Transformations ──▶ Action ──▶  │  Output    │
  │(Lazy)    │    eval     (DAG built)         (.write)     │  Parquet/  │
  └──────────┘                                              │  Delta     │
                                                            └────────────┘

  Execution:
  1. Spark builds DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) of transformations
  2. Catalyst optimizer optimizes the plan
  3. Tungsten engine executes on cluster
  4. Data partitioned across executor nodes
```

### Data Quality Pipeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    DATA QUALITY CHECKS                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Raw Data ──▶ Schema Validation ──▶ Null Check ──▶ Dedup ──▶ Range Check
               ✓ Types correct      ✓ Required     ✓ No     ✓ Values in
               ✓ Columns exist        fields         dups     expected range
               ✗ Fail → Quarantine    not null       found
                                                              │
                                    ┌───── PASS ──────────────┘
                                    ▼
                              Clean Data → Load to Warehouse

                              FAIL → Dead Letter / Quarantine Table
                                     + Alert → Slack/PagerDuty
```

sections.title: 5 Real-World Examples
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Production-grade ETL pipeline with PySpark Processes e-commerce data: orders, users, products
- Reusable transformation functions
- Clean and validate order data
- Join orders with user demographics
- Define schema (always define schema for production)
- Read from multiple sources
- Step 4: Add metadata
- Write to data warehouse (partitioned by date)

**Defines:** `EcommerceTransformer`, `CheckSeverity`, `QualityCheck`, `QualityResult`, `DataQualityFramework`, `TaskStatus`, `Task`, `PipelineDAG`, `extract_orders()`, `extract_users()`

### Example 1: Complete ETL Pipeline with PySpark

```python
"""
Production-grade ETL pipeline with PySpark
Processes e-commerce data: orders, users, products
"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, when, lit, sum as spark_sum, count, avg,
    to_timestamp, date_format, current_timestamp,
    regexp_replace, trim, lower, upper,
    row_number, dense_rank
)
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.types import (
    StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType,
    FloatType, TimestampType, BooleanType
)

# Initialize Spark
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("EcommerceETL") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
    .getOrCreate()

# --- EXTRACT ---
# Define schema (always define schema for production)
orders_schema = StructType([
    StructField("order_id", StringType(), False),
    StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
    StructField("product_id", StringType(), False),
    StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True),
    StructField("price", FloatType(), True),
    StructField("order_date", StringType(), True),
    StructField("status", StringType(), True),
])

# Read from multiple sources
orders_df = spark.read.schema(orders_schema) \
    .option("header", "true") \
    .csv("s3://data-lake/raw/orders/")

users_df = spark.read.format("json") \
    .load("s3://data-lake/raw/users/")

products_df = spark.read.format("parquet") \
    .load("s3://data-lake/raw/products/")

# --- TRANSFORM ---
class EcommerceTransformer:
    """Reusable transformation functions"""

    @staticmethod
    def clean_orders(df):
        """Clean and validate order data"""
        return df \
            .filter(col("order_id").isNotNull()) \
            .filter(col("quantity") > 0) \
            .filter(col("price") > 0) \
            .withColumn("order_date", to_timestamp(col("order_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")) \
            .withColumn("status", upper(trim(col("status")))) \
            .withColumn("total_amount", col("quantity") * col("price")) \
            .dropDuplicates(["order_id"])

    @staticmethod
    def enrich_with_users(orders_df, users_df):
        """Join orders with user demographics"""
        users_clean = users_df.select(
            col("user_id"),
            col("name").alias("user_name"),
            col("email"),
            col("country"),
            col("signup_date")
        )
        return orders_df.join(users_clean, "user_id", "left")

    @staticmethod
    def compute_metrics(df):
        """Compute business metrics"""
        # Daily revenue
        daily_revenue = df \
            .groupBy(date_format("order_date", "yyyy-MM-dd").alias("date")) \
            .agg(
                spark_sum("total_amount").alias("total_revenue"),
                count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
                avg("total_amount").alias("avg_order_value"),
                count("user_id").alias("unique_customers")
            )

        # Top products
        window = Window.orderBy(col("total_sold").desc())
        top_products = df \
            .groupBy("product_id") \
            .agg(
                spark_sum("quantity").alias("total_sold"),
                spark_sum("total_amount").alias("total_revenue")
            ) \
            .withColumn("rank", dense_rank().over(window))

        return daily_revenue, top_products

    @staticmethod
    def add_metadata(df):
        """Add pipeline metadata columns"""
        return df \
            .withColumn("_etl_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("_etl_pipeline", lit("ecommerce_daily_v2"))

# Execute transformations
transformer = EcommerceTransformer()

# Step 1: Clean
orders_clean = transformer.clean_orders(orders_df)

# Step 2: Enrich
orders_enriched = transformer.enrich_with_users(orders_clean, users_df)

# Step 3: Compute
daily_revenue, top_products = transformer.compute_metrics(orders_enriched)

# Step 4: Add metadata
daily_revenue_final = transformer.add_metadata(daily_revenue)

# --- LOAD ---
# Write to data warehouse (partitioned by date)
orders_enriched.write \
    .format("parquet") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .partitionBy("date") \
    .save("s3://data-warehouse/orders_enriched/")

daily_revenue_final.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("append") \
    .save("s3://data-warehouse/daily_revenue/")

top_products.write \
    .format("parquet") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .save("s3://data-warehouse/top_products/")

print("ETL Pipeline completed successfully!")
```

### Example 2: Streaming Pipeline with PySpark Structured Streaming

```python
"""
Real-time streaming pipeline: Kafka → PySpark → Dashboard
Processes clickstream data in real-time
"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    from_json, col, window, count, avg,
    current_timestamp, expr
)
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, TimestampType

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("ClickstreamStreaming") \
    .config("spark.sql.streaming.checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoints") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Schema for clickstream events from Kafka
click_schema = StructType([
    StructField("user_id", StringType()),
    StructField("page", StringType()),
    StructField("action", StringType()),  # click, view, purchase
    StructField("timestamp", StringType()),
    StructField("session_id", StringType()),
    StructField("device", StringType()),
])

# --- READ FROM KAFKA ---
raw_stream = spark.readStream \
    .format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("subscribe", "clickstream") \
    .option("startingOffsets", "latest") \
    .load()

# Parse JSON from Kafka value
parsed_stream = raw_stream \
    .select(from_json(col("value").cast("string"), click_schema).alias("data")) \
    .select("data.*") \
    .withColumn("event_time", col("timestamp").cast(TimestampType()))

# --- REAL-TIME AGGREGATIONS ---

# 1. Page views per minute (tumbling window)
pageviews_per_minute = parsed_stream \
    .withWatermark("event_time", "2 minutes") \
    .groupBy(
        window("event_time", "1 minute"),
        "page"
    ) \
    .agg(
        count("*").alias("view_count"),
        count("user_id").alias("unique_users")
    )

# 2. Active users per 5-minute sliding window
active_users = parsed_stream \
    .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
    .groupBy(
        window("event_time", "5 minutes", "1 minute")  # 5min window, 1min slide
    ) \
    .agg(
        count("user_id").alias("active_users"),
        count("session_id").alias("active_sessions")
    )

# 3. Conversion funnel (view → click → purchase)
conversions = parsed_stream \
    .withWatermark("event_time", "30 minutes") \
    .groupBy(
        window("event_time", "15 minutes"),
        "action"
    ) \
    .count()

# --- WRITE RESULTS ---

# Write to console (for debugging)
query1 = pageviews_per_minute.writeStream \
    .outputMode("update") \
    .format("console") \
    .option("truncate", "false") \
    .start()

# Write to Kafka (for real-time dashboards)
query2 = active_users.writeStream \
    .outputMode("update") \
    .format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("topic", "realtime_metrics") \
    .start()

# Write to Delta Lake (for historical analysis)
query3 = conversions.writeStream \
    .outputMode("append") \
    .format("delta") \
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoints/conversions") \
    .start("s3://data-lake/streaming/conversions/")

# Wait for termination
query1.awaitTermination()
```

### Example 3: Data Quality Framework

```python
"""
Data quality validation framework for pipelines
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Dict, Callable, Optional
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

class CheckSeverity(Enum):
    WARNING = "warning"
    ERROR = "error"
    CRITICAL = "critical"

@dataclass
class QualityCheck:
    name: str
    description: str
    check_fn: Callable
    severity: CheckSeverity = CheckSeverity.ERROR
    threshold: float = 0.0  # Acceptable failure rate

@dataclass
class QualityResult:
    check_name: str
    passed: bool
    total_rows: int
    failed_rows: int
    failure_rate: float
    severity: str
    details: str = ""

class DataQualityFramework:
    """Reusable data quality checks for any pipeline"""

    def __init__(self):
        self.checks: List[QualityCheck] = []
        self.results: List[QualityResult] = []

    def add_check(self, check: QualityCheck):
        self.checks.append(check)

    def run_all(self, data: list) -> Dict:
        """Run all quality checks on data"""
        self.results = []
        total_rows = len(data)

        for check in self.checks:
            failed = [row for row in data if not check.check_fn(row)]
            failure_rate = len(failed) / max(total_rows, 1)
            passed = failure_rate <= check.threshold

            result = QualityResult(
                check_name=check.name,
                passed=passed,
                total_rows=total_rows,
                failed_rows=len(failed),
                failure_rate=failure_rate,
                severity=check.severity.value,
                details=f"Failed rows: {failed[:3]}..." if failed else "All passed"
            )
            self.results.append(result)

        return self.get_summary()

    def get_summary(self) -> Dict:
        total_checks = len(self.results)
        passed = sum(1 for r in self.results if r.passed)
        critical_failures = [r for r in self.results
                            if not r.passed and r.severity == "critical"]

        return {
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "total_checks": total_checks,
            "passed": passed,
            "failed": total_checks - passed,
            "pass_rate": f"{passed / max(total_checks, 1) * 100:.1f}%",
            "critical_failures": len(critical_failures),
            "pipeline_should_proceed": len(critical_failures) == 0,
            "results": [
                {
                    "check": r.check_name,
                    "passed": r.passed,
                    "failed_rows": r.failed_rows,
                    "failure_rate": f"{r.failure_rate * 100:.2f}%",
                    "severity": r.severity
                }
                for r in self.results
            ]
        }

# Build quality checks
dq = DataQualityFramework()

dq.add_check(QualityCheck(
    name="not_null_id",
    description="Order ID must not be null",
    check_fn=lambda row: row.get("order_id") is not None,
    severity=CheckSeverity.CRITICAL,
))

dq.add_check(QualityCheck(
    name="positive_amount",
    description="Amount must be positive",
    check_fn=lambda row: (row.get("amount") or 0) > 0,
    severity=CheckSeverity.ERROR,
))

dq.add_check(QualityCheck(
    name="valid_email",
    description="Email must contain @",
    check_fn=lambda row: "@" in (row.get("email") or ""),
    severity=CheckSeverity.WARNING,
    threshold=0.05  # Allow 5% failures
))

dq.add_check(QualityCheck(
    name="valid_status",
    description="Status must be a known value",
    check_fn=lambda row: row.get("status") in {"pending", "completed", "cancelled"},
    severity=CheckSeverity.ERROR,
))

# Test data
test_data = [
    {"order_id": "O1", "amount": 99.99, "email": "a@b.com", "status": "completed"},
    {"order_id": "O2", "amount": -5.00, "email": "bad_email", "status": "completed"},
    {"order_id": None, "amount": 50.00, "email": "c@d.com", "status": "unknown"},
    {"order_id": "O4", "amount": 25.00, "email": "e@f.com", "status": "pending"},
]

summary = dq.run_all(test_data)
print(f"Pipeline should proceed: {summary['pipeline_should_proceed']}")
for r in summary["results"]:
    status = "✓" if r["passed"] else "✗"
    print(f"  {status} {r['check']}: {r['failure_rate']} failed ({r['severity']})")
```

### Example 4: Data Pipeline Orchestrator

```python
"""
Simple DAG-based pipeline orchestrator (like mini-Airflow)
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Callable, Set
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
import time
import traceback

class TaskStatus(Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    SUCCESS = "success"
    FAILED = "failed"
    SKIPPED = "skipped"

@dataclass
class Task:
    task_id: str
    callable: Callable
    dependencies: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    retries: int = 3
    status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.PENDING
    start_time: float = 0
    end_time: float = 0
    error: str = ""
    result: any = None

class PipelineDAG:
    """DAG-based pipeline orchestrator"""

    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self.tasks: Dict[str, Task] = {}
        self.execution_log: List[dict] = []

    def add_task(self, task_id: str, callable: Callable,
                 dependencies: List[str] = None, retries: int = 3):
        self.tasks[task_id] = Task(
            task_id=task_id,
            callable=callable,
            dependencies=dependencies or [],
            retries=retries
        )

    def execute(self, context: dict = None) -> dict:
        """Execute DAG respecting dependencies"""
        context = context or {}
        start_time = time.time()
        print(f"\n{'='*50}")
        print(f"Pipeline: {self.name}")
        print(f"{'='*50}")

        # Topological sort
        execution_order = self._topological_sort()

        for task_id in execution_order:
            task = self.tasks[task_id]

            # Check dependencies
            deps_met = all(
                self.tasks[dep].status == TaskStatus.SUCCESS
                for dep in task.dependencies
            )

            if not deps_met:
                task.status = TaskStatus.SKIPPED
                print(f"  ⏭ SKIPPED: {task_id} (dependency failed)")
                continue

            # Execute with retries
            task.status = TaskStatus.RUNNING
            task.start_time = time.time()

            for attempt in range(task.retries):
                try:
                    print(f"  ▶ Running: {task_id} (attempt {attempt + 1})")
                    task.result = task.callable(context)
                    task.status = TaskStatus.SUCCESS
                    task.end_time = time.time()
                    duration = task.end_time - task.start_time
                    print(f"  ✓ Success: {task_id} ({duration:.2f}s)")
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    task.error = str(e)
                    if attempt == task.retries - 1:
                        task.status = TaskStatus.FAILED
                        task.end_time = time.time()
                        print(f"  ✗ Failed: {task_id} after {task.retries} attempts - {e}")
                    else:
                        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)  # Backoff

        total_time = time.time() - start_time
        return self._summary(total_time)

    def _topological_sort(self) -> List[str]:
        visited = set()
        order = []

        def dfs(task_id):
            if task_id in visited:
                return
            visited.add(task_id)
            for dep in self.tasks[task_id].dependencies:
                dfs(dep)
            order.append(task_id)

        for task_id in self.tasks:
            dfs(task_id)
        return order

    def _summary(self, total_time: float) -> dict:
        statuses = {s.value: 0 for s in TaskStatus}
        for t in self.tasks.values():
            statuses[t.status.value] += 1

        success = statuses["success"] == len(self.tasks)
        print(f"\n{'='*50}")
        print(f"Pipeline {'SUCCEEDED' if success else 'FAILED'} in {total_time:.2f}s")
        print(f"Tasks: {statuses}")
        return {"success": success, "statuses": statuses, "duration": total_time}

# Build pipeline
pipeline = PipelineDAG("daily_etl")

def extract_orders(ctx):
    ctx["orders"] = [{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}]
    return "Extracted 2 orders"

def extract_users(ctx):
    ctx["users"] = [{"id": "u1"}, {"id": "u2"}]
    return "Extracted 2 users"

def transform(ctx):
    ctx["enriched"] = len(ctx["orders"]) + len(ctx["users"])
    return f"Transformed {ctx['enriched']} records"

def validate(ctx):
    assert ctx["enriched"] > 0
    return "Validation passed"

def load(ctx):
    return f"Loaded {ctx['enriched']} records to warehouse"

pipeline.add_task("extract_orders", extract_orders)
pipeline.add_task("extract_users", extract_users)
pipeline.add_task("transform", transform, dependencies=["extract_orders", "extract_users"])
pipeline.add_task("validate", validate, dependencies=["transform"])
pipeline.add_task("load", load, dependencies=["validate"])

result = pipeline.execute()
```

### Example 5: PySpark Data Warehouse ETL

```python
"""
Star schema data warehouse ETL with PySpark
Builds fact and dimension tables from raw data
"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, lit, when, coalesce, monotonically_increasing_id,
    year, month, dayofmonth, dayofweek, quarter, hour,
    concat_ws, md5, current_timestamp
)

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("DataWarehouseETL").getOrCreate()

class StarSchemaBuilder:
    """Build star schema dimensions and facts"""

    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark

    def build_dim_date(self, start_date: str, end_date: str):
        """Build date dimension table"""
        dates = self.spark.sql(f"""
            SELECT explode(sequence(
                to_date('{start_date}'),
                to_date('{end_date}'),
                interval 1 day
            )) as date
        """)

        return dates \
            .withColumn("date_key", (year("date") * 10000 + month("date") * 100 + dayofmonth("date")).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("year", year("date")) \
            .withColumn("quarter", quarter("date")) \
            .withColumn("month", month("date")) \
            .withColumn("day", dayofmonth("date")) \
            .withColumn("day_of_week", dayofweek("date")) \
            .withColumn("is_weekend", when(dayofweek("date").isin(1, 7), True).otherwise(False))

    def build_dim_customer(self, raw_customers_df):
        """Build customer dimension (SCD Type 2)"""
        return raw_customers_df \
            .withColumn("customer_key", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
            .withColumn("customer_id", col("id")) \
            .withColumn("full_name", concat_ws(" ", col("first_name"), col("last_name"))) \
            .withColumn("email", col("email")) \
            .withColumn("country", col("country")) \
            .withColumn("segment", when(col("total_spent") > 1000, "premium")
                                  .when(col("total_spent") > 100, "regular")
                                  .otherwise("new")) \
            .withColumn("effective_from", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("effective_to", lit(None).cast("timestamp")) \
            .withColumn("is_current", lit(True)) \
            .select("customer_key", "customer_id", "full_name", "email",
                    "country", "segment", "effective_from", "effective_to", "is_current")

    def build_dim_product(self, raw_products_df):
        """Build product dimension"""
        return raw_products_df \
            .withColumn("product_key", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
            .withColumn("product_id", col("id")) \
            .select("product_key", "product_id", "name", "category",
                    "subcategory", "brand", "price")

    def build_fact_orders(self, raw_orders_df, dim_customer_df, dim_product_df):
        """Build fact table by joining with dimensions"""
        # Get surrogate keys from dimensions
        customers = dim_customer_df.filter(col("is_current") == True) \
            .select(col("customer_key"), col("customer_id"))

        products = dim_product_df \
            .select(col("product_key"), col("product_id"))

        # Build fact table
        fact = raw_orders_df \
            .join(customers, raw_orders_df.user_id == customers.customer_id, "left") \
            .join(products, raw_orders_df.product_id == products.product_id, "left") \
            .withColumn("date_key",
                (year("order_date") * 10000 + month("order_date") * 100 + dayofmonth("order_date")).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("order_amount", col("quantity") * col("price")) \
            .withColumn("_etl_loaded_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .select(
                "order_id", "date_key", "customer_key", "product_key",
                "quantity", "price", "order_amount", "status",
                "_etl_loaded_at"
            )

        return fact

    def write_to_warehouse(self, df, table_name: str, partition_cols: list = None):
        """Write to data warehouse with partitioning"""
        writer = df.write.format("parquet").mode("overwrite")
        if partition_cols:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        writer.save(f"s3://data-warehouse/{table_name}/")
        print(f"Wrote {df.count()} rows to {table_name}")
```
